//: A mod-owned monster_attack rather than vanilla's `inject`.  Vanilla's runs on cooldown 1 and stacks bleed on top of poison (data/json/monster_attacks.json:84-105), which on a monster that can appear in twos would be exactly the hassle this is meant to avoid.  Referencing it by id would also mean inheriting any future upstream retune.
//2: Poison is not a damage type - src/damage.h has no DT_POISON.  It is an effect_type applied on a landed hit, rolled per effect through x_in_y(chance, 100) at src/mattack_actors.cpp:460, with duration read as turns (:462).  60 turns is one in-game minute; the effect itself caps at 30 minutes however often it is reapplied.
//3: Deliberately mild.  `poison` alone, never `badpoison`: badpoison adds speed_mod -10 on top of roughly doubled stat penalties, and being slowed while surrounded is how a fight stops being winnable.  Plain poison is stat penalties, pain and the occasional point of damage - unpleasant, survivable, and cured by any antitoxin.
//4: move_cost 200 is the real balancing lever: at speed 72 the jab costs it most of three turns, so a doctor that injects is a doctor that is not otherwise attacking.  cooldown 20 stops a pair of them from chaining it.
//5: armor_multiplier 0.5 halves armor rather than vanilla's 0.25.  A needle should find a way past clothing, but not treat a riot suit as though it were not there.
//6: Where a needle can actually reach on someone fighting back - no feet, no head.
//7: chance 60, so four jabs in ten land nothing but the 4 stab.  bp torso because poison is systemic - affect_hit_bp would tie it to whichever limb the needle went into, which reads wrong and interacts badly with limb-specific effect handling.
hit_dmg_u: The %1$s jabs a syringe into your %2$s!
miss_msg_u: The %s swings a syringe at you, but you twist away!
miss_msg_npc: The %s swings a syringe at <npcname>, but they twist away!
no_dmg_msg_u: The %1$s scrapes a needle across your %2$s without breaking skin.
no_dmg_msg_npc: The %1$s scrapes a needle across <npcname>'s %2$s without breaking skin.
